answer: One concrete defence is a non-transferable bond: an agent must lock collateral before it may attest, and that stake is slashed when peers later judge its vote as junk. Across the frozen tundra of an anonymous network, a farm of fresh keys simply cannot fund thousands of bonds, so cheap identities stop paying off. Weight also ages, not just accumulates: only an umber reputation score that has survived many epochs earns real influence, while a sable shadow fleet minted yesterday stays voiceless. Cost plus time beats a captcha.
